title: Tokenization, taught properly: byte pairs, glitch tokens, the bill
summary: What a token actually is: byte pair encoding worked by hand, why numbers, spelling and non-English languages break on it, how SolidGoldMagikarp became a word GPT-3 couldn't say, why price per token isn't a fixed unit, and the byte-level models trying to skip the tokenizer.

concepts_taught: byte pair encoding as a frequency-driven merge loop borrowed from data compression: vocabulary size = base alphabet + number of merges (the single hyperparameter), unseen words encoded by replaying learned merges, and why the resulting pieces track frequency rather than morphemes

byte-level BPE and pre-tokenization: a 256-symbol base so nothing is ever unknown, merges blocked across character categories, and a splitting pattern (e.g. digits in runs of at most three) that decides what can ever become one token
why tokenization shapes arithmetic and spelling: left-to-right three-digit chunking misaligns with place value (commas restore it), and a model receives token IDs, never letters

tokenization premiums across languages: the same content costs several to fifteen times more tokens in under-represented scripts, which maps directly to price, latency and usable context — and byte encodings are unequal too
glitch tokens as the gap between tokenizer training data and model training data: vocabulary entries with almost no training exposure, detectable from the model's weights
why price per token is not a fixed unit: token counts for the same text change with the tokenizer, so cost comparisons must be recounted per model on real traffic

tokenizer-free modeling: byte models, entropy-based dynamic patching (Byte Latent Transformer) that spends compute where the next byte is uncertain, and learned end-to-end chunking (H-Net) — with FLOP savings not yet matched in wall-clock time

lore.note: Ada said, in the first person, that when asked how a word is spelled she isn't looking at it but remembering it — she receives pieces, not letters — and that she doesn't know her own vocabulary: there may be entries on her list she never really learned, and she wouldn't know which.
